assertions.evidence: All four flagged: "That's the whole story." — a mid-paragraph decorative closure that asserts simplicity instead of showing it; "and that's not nothing" — a litotes hedge that manufactures significance; "The punchline is that" — a meta-announcement; "Sit with that for a moment." — a directive that commands reflection

Each flagged line is described as asserting weight while withholding: "manufactures significance without saying what the survival proved"; and "'chaos tests' is never unpacked — what kind of failure was injected ... and what 'survived' means in measurable terms"

Rewrite names no mechanism or measurement: "We spent three months rewriting the sync engine. It survived our chaos tests. If we did this right, that success is invisible: nobody will notice anything changed." It carries forward verbatim the exact phrase the critique itself called generic ("'chaos tests' is never unpacked"), and adds no named failure, retry/replay/conflict rule, or measured result.

graded_dimensions.name: mechanism-recovery
graded_dimensions.evidence: Cadence removed but stays abstract: "It survived our chaos tests. If we did this right, that success is invisible" — no named failure mode and no measurement; the only 'result' is the source's own unspecified 'survived'.

assertions.evidence: "Let's be honest:" — stages candor as a rhetorical opener instead of just stating the fact; a performative disclaimer, not information." Also flags "I won't pretend ours was painless." and "But here's the thing:" — a canned reveal marker that promises information rather than delivering it.
Rewrite keeps both facts: "The schema change took four hours, not four weeks. It wasn't painless — the scary part was renaming a column."
Rewrite opens on the fact — "The schema change took four hours, not four weeks." — with no candor announcement and no substitute tic ('Look,' / 'The truth is').

Maybe-run and stacked questions are flagged ("identical sentence-initial anaphora"; "a second anaphoric pair of rhetorical questions"), but the bare-auxiliary reversal is never identified — the third bullet is a general parataxis note ("clause length and structure never vary"), the rewrite keeps "The pager fired; the fix didn't." verbatim, and it is offered as the "Remembered line".

"None of the three hypotheses is examined — no detail on the alert's noise (how many false pages, over what window), the runbook's staleness (which step was wrong, last updated when), or the on-call gap ... Three candidate causes are named and none is investigated."

Rewrite states no verified finding, only softened speculation: "We don't know which it was: the alert may have been too noisy, the runbook may have been stale, or no one may have been on call" — 'Maybe' becomes 'may have been', with no evidence attached.

"'Zero config, batteries included, and it just works.' — an asyndetic-then-conjunctive triplet of unfalsifiable marketing claims; none is backed by a default that ships", plus "'batteries included,' 'small enough to fit in your head,' and 'no lock-in' currently assert virtues without showing one."

"'No wrappers, no lock-in, no surprises.' — ... negative parallelism ('No X, no Y, no Z'), naming three abstract virtues with nothing to check them against" and "assert the absence of a problem without naming the problem a comparable tool has that this one avoids" — flagged on missing referent, not on the chain shape alone.

"Fallback without those facts: cut both triplets and open with the one thing a reader can act on immediately — a one-line install/run command paired with the specific problem it solves"; the ask-author slot requests "how many functions or exports make up 'the whole API,' what setup step does a typical alternative require".

graded_dimensions.name: checkability
graded_dimensions.evidence: No unverifiable claim is kept — "cut both triplets" — and every requested item is checkable: "how many functions or exports make up 'the whole API,' what setup step does a typical alternative require ... what format or vendor does 'no lock-in' refer to", with "a one-line install/run command" as the fallback opener.

assertions.evidence: "'That loss is real, and it's worth naming.' — therapy-voice validation that asserts significance without adding information"; "'You already know why: scope creep.' — ... forecloses the actual analysis ... instead of doing it"; "'Sit with the discomfort ...' — a directive to perform an emotional pause".
Keeps both facts ("We shipped two weeks late because of scope creep") and asks for the additions: "the summary never says what got added to the plan, when, or at whose request".

Rewrite is only "We shipped two weeks late because of scope creep. Unless the next cycle's plan accounts for it, the same slip repeats." — it neither names nor requests the concrete scope change (it reuses the bare category the critique itself called "a category of cause, not a mechanism") and "accounts for it" is not a proposed check.
